episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 13, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 13, 2026

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. Last week the chip equity market and the memory contract market handed down opposite verdicts on whether AI demand actually lasts. This week's prints from ASML and TSMC start to settle which one had it right.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 13, 2026

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's today's thesis. Security demand has just shown up in reseller channel data, but the gains are concentrating in a few platforms. Those same platforms are becoming the trusted distribution channel for enterprise AI. That's concentration, not a rising tide.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. The AI buildout is outgrowing bank balance sheets, and banks are now trying to hand that risk to non-banks just as the market marks the anchor tenant's credit down.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has asked one question. Who, if anyone, is pricing private equity at arm's length? The secondaries market has now answered, and the answer splits by asset quality.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: four banks have spent more than six months unable to offload thirty-eight billion dollars of construction debt tied to a single Oracle-leased data-center project, because AI-linked exposure is bumping against their own internal limits.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 15, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 15, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis up front. The energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine is over. The more revealing story isn't that it broke. It's whom Washington leaned on to try to hold it together.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 15, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the shape of the week. The two companies furthest upstream in the chip supply chain, ASML and TSMC, both just reported record quarters. episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 15, 2026
episodes.summary: One quick disclosure up front. Anthropic makes the model behind this show, and our lead item today is an Anthropic product. Here's the thread running through everything we're covering. Agents are being built to run longer, remember more, and now spend money on their own.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 15, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the AI stack is getting repriced from both ends at once. Credit markets are questioning who actually pays for the compute capacity being built. Equity markets are questioning whether the frontier labs will eat the software sitting on top of it.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 15, 2026
episodes.summary: For the first time this week, a big pharma company paid for AI-picked biology, not AI-optimized chemistry. That's the headline. It paid on the same option terms as every other AI deal. And on the same day, the public market was asked to fund two AI-native biotechs in cash, against much thinner evidence.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 15, 2026

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 15, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: stress in AI financing is climbing the quality ladder, with Oracle's credit-default swaps widening to a record 288 basis points overnight in the same week the IMF proposed bank capital charges aimed at AI and private-credit exposure.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 15, 2026

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 15, 2026

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 15, 2026

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 16, 2026

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 16, 2026

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 16, 2026

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 16, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 17, 2026

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 17, 2026

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 17, 2026

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 17, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 18, 2026

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 18, 2026

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 18, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 19, 2026

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 19, 2026

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 19, 2026
episodes.summary: On Thursday we covered Recursion Pharmaceuticals' $200 million raise and Sanofi's option exercise as capital-markets news. What we skipped was the clinical data that came out the same morning. That data is the more important story.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 20, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 20, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thesis is simple. In rare earths and on the American grid alike, the deal everyone is talking about is not yet written in the instrument that actually binds. Two stories, one pattern. Washington has announced a rare earth date that Beijing hasn't written into law.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 20, 2026

Today we have one model you can own outright, and one verifier you can point at your own work. Then there's a counter-example, where the vendor swaps the model under you without asking.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 20, 2026
episodes.summary: The scarce resource in enterprise AI has quietly shifted. It used to be capability: could the agent do the task. Now it's permission: who is allowed to let it. On Monday, three vendors moved to own one permission gate each. A fourth recently did the same at the developer layer. That's the spine of today's briefing.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 20, 2026
episodes.summary: Two things happened in the past week that come at the same question from opposite directions. A frontier AI lab says it wants to own the robot body, not just supply the brain.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 20, 2026

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 21, 2026

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the frame. Through Tuesday, two markets that had been flashing stress all month went quiet. Equity volatility relaxed, and so did the long end of the Treasury curve. Credit, on the latest data through Monday, did not. That divergence is today's story.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: For two days this desk told you bitcoin's institutional owners were stepping back. The read was that the ETF wrapper had been a net seller all month and that no new owner had shown up. On Monday, they stepped in.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's today's thesis. Washington is loosening the legal limits on Russian energy at the same moment Ukraine is tightening the physical ones. The market's reaction so far tells you which force it believes, and it may be pricing the wrong one.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. Last week, Seoul's equity market priced memory as a cyclical peak. The price evidence that has arrived since then points the other way. Forecasters are raising their contract-price calls. Samsung is asking roughly triple today's HBM pricing for next year's product.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis. The agent race has stopped being about the model and started being about the delivery channel. Today we have an integrator putting headcount behind agent production, a governed platform built for the most risk-averse buyer in the economy, and a lab handing its AI office tools to every user.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: The theme today is concentration. Enterprises keep moving more of their critical operations, and more of their workflow automation, onto fewer platforms. The last few days tested both sides of that bet. One test was what it costs when a platform breaks. The other was what it actually returns when it works.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: In the space of five days, AstraZeneca has handed us a tidy natural experiment in how pharma actually prices AI. It wrote binding cash for the AI that's hardest to prove. It offered only a handshake for the AI that's easiest to measure. That inversion is today's lead.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thesis is simple. The one robotics business with audited, multi-year unit economics just showed what scale looks like. And even that business is cutting price to keep growing.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's frame is simple. SpaceX's first profitable quarter as a public company was an AI quarter, not a rocket quarter.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: For the better part of a week, this show has been counting deals in one direction only. Capital has gone into new take-privates, and nothing signed has come out the other side to a genuine third-party buyer. That pattern just got its first real test, and the test failed.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 21, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: credit kept widening underneath the AI buildout while stocks calmed, and a marquee AI-infrastructure exit, Blackstone's AirTrunk listing, was reportedly pulled instead of clearing on the sponsor's terms.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: Last week the tape was about AI credit. This week the pressure is coming from somewhere else. It is coming from the long end of the Treasury curve, and from outside the United States.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 22, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis. After weeks of hyperscalers bidding for power plants that already exist, one is now putting its name on new nuclear. But it's a target, not a build. And the same gap between an announced deal and a binding transfer runs through Washington's negotiation over Lukoil's foreign assets.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: The thesis today is simple. In a supply-bound chip market, power sits with whoever allocates the scarce part. This week gave us two new stories where that allocator is Nvidia, not Washington and not the customer's checkbook. Meanwhile, the equity tape kept pricing the opposite problem.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thread running through today's briefing. AI products are shifting from tools you invoke to jobs that keep running in the background. At the same time, buying a frontier model is becoming a cloud-neutral line item rather than a single-vendor commitment.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: Two incumbent software vendors reported yesterday, and both are building AI-linked backlog that their own cash generation can fund. Underneath them, the infrastructure layer is still signing backlog ahead of the money needed to build it. So today's organizing question isn't how big a vendor's AI backlog is.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: This week, the AI drug-design layer repriced itself on numbers no outsider can check. The clearest case is Isomorphic Labs. It's the right place to open, because it answers a question this show has been asking all week.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 22, 2026

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis. Private credit's stress is landing on equity before it lands on lenders. A survey of business development company results, published this week, shows where the squeeze is going. And the Fed's new data tell us why that is the system working as designed, not breaking down.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week now, this show has been counting capital going into take-privates. On the other side of the ledger, there's still no signed sale of a sponsor-held company to a genuine third-party buyer. Today brings the biggest entry yet, and the first one two mega-sponsors visibly fought over.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 22, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: Amazon put its name on new nuclear generation, twelve small modular reactors in Indiana with X-energy and AEP, but it's a development target, not a construction permit.
